attachments.text:
# Row Level Security (RLS) for SaySo Aurora PostgreSQL

This document outlines the Row Level Security strategy for the SaySo database, enabling fine-grained access control based on Cognito authentication and user roles.

## Overview

RLS enforces data access policies at the database level, ensuring users can only access data they're authorized to see regardless of application-level bugs or misconfigurations.

### Authentication Flow

```
┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────────┐
│   Mobile    │────▶│   Cognito   │────▶│   Lambda    │────▶│   Aurora    │
│    App      │     │    JWT      │     │  Resolver   │     │  (RLS)      │
└─────────────┘     └─────────────┘     └─────────────┘     └─────────────┘
                          │                    │
                          │                    ▼
                          │              SET app.current_user_id
                          └─────────────▶SET app.current_user_role

```

### User Roles

| Role    | Description     | Permissions                                              |
| ------- | --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| VIEWER  | Standard user   | Read public content, manage own profile and interactions |
| CREATOR | Content creator | All Viewer permissions + create/manage posts             |
| ADMIN   | Administrator   | Full access to all data and moderation tools             |

---

## Session Context

RLS policies rely on PostgreSQL session variables set at connection time from the authenticated Cognito JWT.

### Required Session Variables

| Variable              | Type | Source         | Description               |
| --------------------- | ---- | -------------- | ------------------------- |
| app.current_user_id   | uuid | JWT sub claim  | Cognito user identifier   |
| app.current_user_role | text | users.userRole | User's role from database |

### Setting Context in Lambda

async function executeWithRLS(
  cognitoSub: string,
  userRole: string,
  query: string,
  params: any[]
) {
  const client = await pool.connect();
  try {
    await client.query('BEGIN');
    // SET LOCAL scopes to current transaction only
    await client.query(`SET LOCAL app.current_user_id = $1`, [cognitoSub]);
    await client.query(`SET LOCAL app.current_user_role = $1`, [userRole]);

    const result = await client.query(query, params);
    await client.query('COMMIT');
    return result;
  } catch (e) {
    await client.query('ROLLBACK');
    throw e;
  } finally {
    client.release();
  }
}

---

## Helper Functions

These functions simplify policy definitions and centralize identity logic.

### `current_user_id()`

Returns the internal `users.id` UUID for the authenticated Cognito user.

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION current_user_id()
RETURNS uuid AS $$
  SELECT id FROM users
  WHERE "cognitoId" = current_setting('app.current_user_id', true)::uuid
$$ LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY DEFINER;

*Note*: `SECURITY DEFINER` allows this function to query `users` even if the calling user doesn't have direct access.

### `is_admin()`

Returns `true` if the current user has the ADMIN role.

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION is_admin()
RETURNS boolean AS $$
  SELECT current_setting('app.current_user_role', true) = 'ADMIN'
$$ LANGUAGE sql STABLE;

### `is_creator_or_admin()`

Returns `true` if the current user is a CREATOR or ADMIN.

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION is_creator_or_admin()
RETURNS boolean AS $$
  SELECT current_setting('app.current_user_role', true) IN ('CREATOR', 'ADMIN')
$$ LANGUAGE sql STABLE;

---

## Policy Categories

Tables are grouped into categories based on their access patterns.

### Category A: User-Owned Private Data

*Tables*: `users`, `userSocialLinks`, `userFollows`, `topicFollows`, `deviceTokens`, `userSettings`, `dailyDigests`, `dailyDigestPosts`, `exploreFeeds`, `exploreFeedPosts`

*Access Pattern*:

• Users have full access to their own records
• Admins have full access to all records
• No cross-user visibility (except for specific cases like public profiles)

| Operation | Viewer   | Creator  | Admin |
| --------- | -------- | -------- | ----- |
| SELECT    | Own only | Own only | All   |
| INSERT    | Own only | Own only | All   |
| UPDATE    | Own only | Own only | All   |
| DELETE    | Own only | Own only | All   |

*Special Case - `users` table*:

• Public profile fields (name, username, bio, profilePictureUrl) should be readable by all authenticated users for features like following and viewing creator profiles
• Sensitive fields (email, phoneNumber, cognitoId) remain private

### Category B: Content with Public Read Access

*Tables*: `posts`, `media`, `comments`

*Access Pattern*:

• Published/approved content is readable by all authenticated users
• Owners can read their own drafts and unpublished content
• Only owners (creators) can create and modify their content
• Admins have full access for moderation

| Operation | Viewer         | Creator         | Admin |
| --------- | -------------- | --------------- | ----- |
| SELECT    | Published only | Published + Own | All   |
| INSERT    | -              | Own only        | All   |
| UPDATE    | -              | Own only        | All   |
| DELETE    | -              | -               | All   |

*Post Visibility Rules*:

• `status = 'PUBLISHED'` → Visible to all
• `status IN ('DRAFT', 'PROCESSING')` → Visible to owner only
• `status IN ('ARCHIVED', 'REJECTED', 'DELETED')` → Visible to owner and admin
• `banned = true` → Visible to admin only

### Category C: User Interactions

*Tables*: `postLikes`, `postSaves`, `postShares`, `postCommentLikes`

*Access Pattern*:

• All interactions are publicly readable (for counts and "liked by" features)
• Users can only create/delete their own interactions
• No updates (interactions are immutable)

| Operation | Viewer   | Creator  | Admin |
| --------- | -------- | -------- | ----- |
| SELECT    | All      | All      | All   |
| INSERT    | Own only | Own only | All   |
| UPDATE    | -        | -        | -     |
| DELETE    | Own only | Own only | All   |

### Category D: Reference/Lookup Data

*Tables*: `topics`, `topicGroups`, `trendingTopics`, `sources`, `globalDigests`, `topicDigests`, `topicDigestPosts`, `globalDigestPosts`, `postTopics`, `postSources`

*Access Pattern*:

• Readable by all authenticated users
• Only admins can modify

| Operation | Viewer | Creator | Admin |
| --------- | ------ | ------- | ----- |
| SELECT    | All    | All     | All   |
| INSERT    | -      | -       | All   |
| UPDATE    | -      | -       | All   |
| DELETE    | -      | -       | All   |

*Exception - `postTopics` and `postSources`*:

• Creators can manage associations for their own posts

### Category E: Admin-Only Tables

*Tables*: `contentModerationQueue`, `processSteps`

*Access Pattern*:

• Only admins can access these tables
• Used for content moderation and internal processing

| Operation | Viewer | Creator | Admin |
| --------- | ------ | ------- | ----- |
| SELECT    | -      | -       | All   |
| INSERT    | -      | -       | All   |
| UPDATE    | -      | -       | All   |
| DELETE    | -      | -       | All   |

---

## Detailed Policy Definitions

### Category A: User-Owned Private Data

#### `users`

ALTER TABLE users ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE users FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

-- Public profile visibility for all authenticated users
CREATE POLICY users_select_public ON users
  FOR SELECT
  USING (
    is_admin()
    OR "cognitoId" = current_setting('app.current_user_id', true)::uuid
    OR deleted = false  -- Allow viewing non-deleted user profiles
  );

-- Only own profile or admin can update
CREATE POLICY users_update ON users
  FOR UPDATE
  USING (
    is_admin()
    OR "cognitoId" = current_setting('app.current_user_id', true)::uuid
  );

-- Only admin can delete (soft delete via update preferred)
CREATE POLICY users_delete ON users
  FOR DELETE
  USING (is_admin());

<@U06JQHRF6HJ> <@U06TP3HRUKV> and FYI <@U08SFKMBSMR>

We should adapt a hybrid approach for app sync resolvers.

AWS supports JS resolvers that run in AppSync's runtime (no Lambda).

```// resolver.js
export function request(ctx) {
  return { operation: 'Query', sql: `SELECT * FROM Users WHERE username = :username`, ...}
}```
For simple queries, like `checkUsername` this approach is perfect.

For complex scenarios like mutations, transactions etc, we'll have to use lambda resolvers. Since many of queries will be readonly, Appsync JS resolvers will be fast and lightweight.

attachments.text:
Media state machine completes  
│  
▼  
EmitMediaReady Lambda ──► (IMAGE, VIDEO, TEXT caption) → SendMessageBatch to SQS  
│  
▼  
ModerationQueue (SQS)  
│  
▼  
process-moderation Lambda (SQS consumer) ──► One job per invocation  
│  
│  
│  
▼  
EventBridge: ModerationCompleted  
│  
├── moderationStatus === ACCEPTED ──► publish-post Lambda  
│  
└── REJECTED / PENDING_REVIEW ──► No publish; client shows status
For carousels we do a rollup on the media items, so if a media is accepted from nima only then we publish

:thread: Media Processing Pipeline
Changes I think we should make
• Have 2 appsync resolvers, 1 which can return presigned URLs for client to upload files, another to kickstart the process after files have been uploaded which can return postID, so client can track the actual post, this will also remove save file out of the pipeline
• Decouple post and media from the pipeline, this will enable running tagging/moderation parallel to save processing time.
• Tag all media/process with `postId::mediaID`  so we can track things better.
• Add additional metadata like caption, postId to CF uploads
• Add monitoring so we can get slack update or email if something fails.
• I am still debating whether to keep the media processing as a state machine or make it queue based, i do like the UI that comes with state machines but right now the wiring feels like a lot.

I was able to configure pgAdmin to connect to prod DB. Notice the red background to remind me I'm playing with fire :D

attachments.title: <https://github.com/the-news-movement/tnm-aws-platform/blob/main/scripts/bastion-tunnel.sh|bastion-tunnel.sh>
attachments.text:
```
#!/bin/bash
# Opens an SSM port-forwarding tunnel to Aurora PostgreSQL via the bastion host.
# Prerequisites: AWS CLI v2, Session Manager plugin, AWS_PROFILE exported and logged in.
#
# Usage:
#   export AWS_PROFILE=stg-readonly   # or prod-readonly
#   aws sso login
#   ./scripts/bastion-tunnel.sh [local_port]

set -euo pipefail

LOCAL_PORT="${1:-5432}"
SSM_PORT=$((LOCAL_PORT + 1))

cleanup() {
  echo ""
  echo "Shutting down..."
  kill $(jobs -p) 2>/dev/null
  wait 2>/dev/null
}
trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM

if [[ -z "${AWS_PROFILE:-}" ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: AWS_PROFILE is not set. Export it first, e.g.:"
  echo "  export AWS_PROFILE=stg-readonly"
  exit 1
fi

echo "Using AWS_PROFILE=$AWS_PROFILE"

echo "Fetching bastion instance ID..."
INSTANCE_ID=$(aws ssm get-parameter \
  --name "/sayso/bastion/instance-id" \
  --query 'Parameter.Value' \
  --output text)

echo "Fetching RDS Proxy endpoint..."
DB_HOST=$(aws ssm get-parameter \
  --name "/sayso/database/proxy-endpoint" \
  --query 'Parameter.Value' \
  --output text)

echo "Fetching database credentials..."
SECRET_ARN=$(aws ssm get-parameter \
  --name "/sayso/database/secret-arn" \
  --query 'Parameter.Value' \
  --output text)

DB_USER=$(aws secretsmanager get-secret-value \
  --secret-id "$SECRET_ARN" \
  --query SecretString \
  --output text | jq -r .username)

echo ""
echo "========================================="
echo " Tunnel ready to start"
echo "========================================="
echo " Host (in pgAdmin): 127.0.0.1"
echo " Port:              $LOCAL_PORT"
echo " Database:          sayso"
echo " Username:          $DB_USER"
echo " SSL Mode:          require"
echo ""
echo " Password: run this in another terminal:"
echo "   aws secretsmanager get-secret-value \\"
echo "     --secret-id \"$SECRET_ARN\" \\"
echo "     --query SecretString --output text | jq -r .password"
echo "========================================="
echo ""
echo "Starting SSM tunnel on 0.0.0.0:$LOCAL_PORT (Ctrl+C to stop)..."

# SSM tunnel binds to 127.0.0.1 only, so we use socat to relay from 0.0.0.0
# This allows Windows pgAdmin to reach the tunnel running inside WSL.
aws ssm start-session \
  --target "$INSTANCE_ID" \
  --document-name AWS-StartPortForwardingSessionToRemoteHost \
  --parameters "{\"host\":[\"$DB_HOST\"],\"portNumber\":[\"5432\"],\"localPortNumber\":[\"$SSM_PORT\"]}" &

# Wait for SSM tunnel to be ready
sleep 3

echo "Starting socat relay 0.0.0.0:$LOCAL_PORT -> 127.0.0.1:$SSM_PORT..."
socat TCP-LISTEN:$LOCAL_PORT,fork,reuseaddr,bind=0.0.0.0 TCP:127.0.0.1:$SSM_PORT

```

attachments.title: #151 refactor: separate stacks & infra isolation
attachments.text:
*Overview*

This PR refactors the monolithic CDK infrastructure into independent, isolated stacks with strict boundary enforcement. The goal is to enable independent deployments, reduce blast radius, and prevent accidental cross-stack coupling.

*Key Changes*

*:building_construction: Architecture Refactoring*

*Stack Separation*
• Split monolithic stack into 8 independent stacks:  
   • `platform-networking` - VPC, subnets, NAT gateways  
   • `platform-vpc-endpoints` - VPC Interface and Gateway endpoints  
   • `platform-sayso-auth` - Cognito (no networking dependencies)  
   • `platform-sayso-search` - OpenSearch Serverless  
   • `platform-sayso-database` - Aurora PostgreSQL  
   • `platform-sayso-ml` - SageMaker endpoints and training  
   • `platform-sayso-pipeline` - Kinesis/Glue/Athena  
   • `platform-kudosbot` - KudosBot infrastructure
*Cross-Stack Communication*
• Stacks communicate via CloudFormation exports (`Fn.importValue()`)
• CDC integration uses deterministic role naming to avoid circular dependencies
• No runtime cross-stack references needed (stacks are fully independent)

*:lock: Network Isolation*

*Dedicated Subnets*
• Created dedicated VPC Endpoint subnets (`/27` CIDR blocks) owned by NetworkingStack
• Project-specific subnet allocations (Sayso: `/24`, KudosBot: `/28`)
• Aurora and SageMaker get dedicated isolated subnets
*S3 Gateway Endpoint Fix*
• Changed from `SubnetType` enum to explicit subnet selections
• Prevents arbitrary subnet selection at deployment time
• Added `privateSubnetsForS3` and `isolatedSubnetsForS3` props to NetworkingStackProps
*Configurable Availability Zones*
• Moved hardcoded AZs to environment configuration
• Supports 2-3 AZ deployments based on region

*:shield: Security Improvements*

*CDC Consumer IAM*
• Removed invalid `aoss:collection` IAM condition (not a valid OpenSearch Serverless condition key)
• Scoped IAM resources to account/region: `arn:aws:aoss:${Aws.REGION}:${Aws.ACCOUNT_ID}:collection/*`
• Added CDC consumer role to OpenSearch data access policy
*OpenSearch Access Policy*
• Added `additionalWriterRoleArns` prop for cross-stack role authorization

attachments.title: #281 feat: resolve full media URLs server-side & add custom CDN domain :sparkles:
attachments.text:
*Summary*

This change moves media URL resolution to the backend so the iOS app no longer has to assemble URLs client-side.

*Media URL resolution*

• `mapPostToGraphQL` now converts `rawAssetUrl` into a full CloudFront URL and returns it as `streamUrl`.
• Image posts now return a usable URL like  
`<https://cdn.svc.sayso.news/posts/>...` instead of `null`.
• Video posts remain unchanged and continue returning Cloudflare HLS URLs.
• `rawAssetUrl` is still returned for backward compatibility.
• All 7 resolvers that use `mapPostToGraphQL` were updated to pass `cloudfrontBaseUrl`.

*Custom CDN domain*

CloudFront now uses a proper domain instead of the default `*.<http://cloudfront.net|cloudfront.net>`.
Domains by environment:
• *prod* → `cdn.svc.sayso.news`
• *stg* → `cdn.stg.svc.sayso.news`
• *dev* → `cdn-dev.stg.svc.sayso.news`
PR environments are intentionally skipped to avoid the overhead of creating and cleaning up ACM certificates.
The setup includes:
• ACM certificate with DNS validation
• Route53 alias record pointing to the distribution
All of this is provisioned automatically.

*Infrastructure impact*

No additional infra changes were required.
• `MEDIA_CLOUDFRONT_URL` is already configured on all AppSync lambdas.
• The new domain flows through automatically via the existing SSM parameter and AppConfig setup.

*iOS impact*

Once this is deployed, the iOS app can stop resolving image URLs manually.
`resolvePictureURL` can be removed and the app can simply use `streamUrl` for both images and videos.

*Test plan*

• Deploy to *dev* and confirm `streamUrl` returns full URLs like  
`<https://cdn-dev.stg.svc.sayso.news/>...` for image posts
• Verify video posts still return Cloudflare HLS URLs in `streamUrl`
• Confirm the ACM certificate validates successfully
• Verify the custom CDN domain resolves correctly
• Check AppConfig and confirm `cloudfrontUrl` reflects the new domain

attachments.text:
1. Close stale release PRs — Before creating/updating the release PR, close any open PRs from different release/v* branches (with a comment + branch deletion). Prevents duplicate PRs and version regression.
2. Extract release notes from CHANGELOG.md instead of regenerating — The publish-release job was calling generate-release-notes again at publish time, but the tag hadn't been created yet so it computed notes from the previous tag, which could include commits from a different version range. Now it reads the changelog entry directly from CHANGELOG.md, which was already correctly written during the create-release-pr job.

Ohhh wait - I only added caching step to PR stacks - lemme add those to stg/prod workflows. So the way it'll work is:

• *Cache hit* (source unchanged): CDK finds the previous `cdk.out` with pre-built assets. It computes the asset hash for each Lambda, finds a matching asset directory already present, and skips esbuild bundling entirely. Deploy just uploads the unchanged CloudFormation template (which itself detects no change and skips the Lambda update).
• *Cache miss* (source changed): The `hashFiles('src/**', 'lib/**', ...)` key changes, so no exact match. The restore-keys fallback restores the closest previous `cdk.out`, meaning only the functions whose source actually changed need rebundling — the rest reuse cached assets.
• *Full cache bust*: Changing `pnpm-lock.yaml` (new dependency) invalidates the entire cache, triggering a full rebuild.

<@U09FVDA7NEQ> <@U06TP3HRUKV> Please give a quick look at this and let me know if you have any thoughts.

```SaySo: Redesign & Architecture Recommendations
Current State Summary
The app is in decent shape: 100% SwiftUI, MVVM-ish, coordinator navigation, custom AppSync GraphQL client, solid video infrastructure. But there are patterns that will hurt you at scale:

Singleton services everywhere — untestable, tightly coupled, hard to scope
No domain layer — ViewModels call services directly, mixing data fetching, business logic, and UI state
No design token system — colors/spacing/typography defined ad-hoc per view
Manual GraphQL response types — no codegen means drift risk and boilerplate
@ObservableObject + @Published — older pattern, verbose, less performant than what's available now
1. Target Architecture: Clean Architecture + @Observable
The cleanest separation for your stack is three layers:


┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│            PRESENTATION LAYER           │
│   Views (SwiftUI) + ViewModels          │
│   @Observable, no business logic        │
├─────────────────────────────────────────┤
│              DOMAIN LAYER               │
│   Use Cases / Interactors               │
│   Pure Swift, no framework deps         │
├─────────────────────────────────────────┤
│               DATA LAYER                │
│   Repositories (protocols)              │
│   GraphQL DataSource + Local DataSource │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
Why Use Cases
Right now PostService does everything: fetch, cache, map, interact (like/save/comment), de-duplicate, subscribe. A Use Case breaks that apart:


// Domain layer — pure Swift, no AppSync, no SwiftUI
protocol FeedUseCaseProtocol {
    func fetchDigest(for userId: String) async throws -> [Post]
    func fetchExploreFeed(page: String?) async throws -> ([Post], nextPage: String?)
}

struct FeedUseCase: FeedUseCaseProtocol {
    private let postRepository: PostRepositoryProtocol
    private let digestRepository: DigestRepositoryProtocol
    
    func fetchDigest(for userId: String) async throws -> [Post] {
        let digest = try await digestRepository.fetchLatest(userId: userId)
        return try await postRepository.fetchPosts(ids: digest.postIds)
    }
}
This means your ViewModel becomes just UI state management:


@Observable
final class FeedViewModel {
    var posts: [Post] = []
    var isLoading = false
    var error: AppError?
    
    private let feedUseCase: FeedUseCaseProtocol
    
    init(feedUseCase: FeedUseCaseProtocol) { // Injected, not .shared
        self.feedUseCase = feedUseCase
    }
    
    func load() async {
        isLoading = true
        defer { isLoading = false }
        do {
            posts = try await feedUseCase.fetchDigest(for: currentUserId)
        } catch {
            self.error = AppError(from: error)
        }
    }
}
2. GraphQL: Switch to Apollo iOS
Your current custom AppSyncClient works but has two big problems: no compile-time query validation, and manual response types that can drift from the schema. Apollo iOS with codegen solves both.


# apollo-codegen generates this from your .graphql files:
query GetDigest($userId: ID!, $date: String!) {
    getDigest(userId: $userId, date: $date) {
        id
        title
        postIds
    }
}
Apollo generates GetDigestQuery with typed response models. Your GraphQL data source then becomes:


struct GraphQLPostDataSource: PostRemoteDataSourceProtocol {
    private let client: ApolloClient
    
    func fetchPosts(ids: [String]) async throws -> [GQLPost] {
        try await client.fetch(query: GetPostsByIdsQuery(ids: ids))
            .data?.posts.compactMap { $0 } ?? []
    }
}
If switching Apollo feels like too much disruption upfront, at minimum add protocol wrappers over your current AppSyncClient so you can swap it later without touching ViewModels.

3. Dependency Injection: Drop the Singletons
Replace PostService.shared pattern with constructor injection + an AppContainer at the root:


// App root — owns all dependencies
@main
struct SaySoApp: App {
    let container = AppContainer()
    
    var body: some Scene {
        WindowGroup {
            AppRoutes()
                .environment(container.authViewModel)
                .environment(container.videoPlaybackManager)
        }
    }
}

final class AppContainer {
    // Infrastructure
    let apolloClient: ApolloClient = makeApolloClient()
    
    // Data sources
    lazy var postDataSource: PostRemoteDataSourceProtocol = GraphQLPostDataSource(client: apolloClient)
    
    // Repositories
    lazy var postRepository: PostRepositoryProtocol = PostRepository(remoteSource: postDataSource)
    
    // Use cases
    lazy var feedUseCase: FeedUseCaseProtocol = FeedUseCase(postRepository: postRepository, ...)
    
    // ViewModels (created fresh, not stored)
    func makeFeedViewModel() -> FeedViewModel {
        FeedViewModel(feedUseCase: feedUseCase)
    }
}
4. @Observable Instead of ObservableObject
iOS 17+ @Observable is the modern replacement. It's more performant (views only re-render for properties they actually read) and less boilerplate:


// Before
final class ProfileViewModel: ObservableObject {
    @Published var user: UIUser?
    @Published var posts: [UIPost] = []
    @Published var isLoading = false
}

// After — no @Published needed
@Observable
final class ProfileViewModel {
    var user: UIUser?
    var posts: [UIPost] = []
    var isLoading = false
}

// In views
@State private var viewModel = ProfileViewModel(...)  // Not @StateObject
Since this is iOS 17+ only, check your deployment target. If you're supporting iOS 16, you can adopt @Observable alongside a compatibility shim or just accept the migration is forward-looking.

5. Design System First — Before Touching Any View
This is the most important thing to do before redesigning any screen. Build a design token system:


SharedUI/
  DesignSystem/
    Tokens/
      Colors.swift         ← SaySoColor.primary, .surface, .textPrimary, etc.
      Typography.swift     ← SaySoFont.headline, .body, .caption, etc.
      Spacing.swift        ← SaySoSpacing.xs (4), .sm (8), .md (16), .lg (24), etc.
      BorderRadius.swift   ← <http://SaySoRadius.sm|SaySoRadius.sm>, .md, .card, .pill
    Components/
      Buttons/
        PrimaryButton.swift
        GhostButton.swift
        IconButton.swift
      Media/
        VideoThumbnailView.swift
        AvatarView.swift
      Inputs/
        SearchField.swift
      Feed/
        PostCardView.swift     ← used in both explore and digest
        PostActionBar.swift    ← likes/saves/comments/share row
Define everything in one place:


// Tokens/Colors.swift
extension Color {
    static let saySoPrimary     = Color("Primary")
    static let saySoSurface     = Color("Surface")
    static let saySoBackground  = Color("Background")
    static let saySoTextPrimary = Color("TextPrimary")
}

// Tokens/Spacing.swift
enum SaySoSpacing {
    static let xs: CGFloat  = 4
    static let sm: CGFloat  = 8
    static let md: CGFloat  = 16
    static let lg: CGFloat  = 24
    static let xl: CGFloat  = 32
    static let xxl: CGFloat = 48
}
You will thank yourself for this when you need to update the color palette or spacing system later.

6. Video Architecture: Formalize What You Have
Your video stack is actually well-designed. The main improvement is to make VideoPlaybackManager injectable (not a singleton) and define a protocol:


protocol VideoPlaybackManaging: AnyObject {
    var isMuted: Bool { get set }
    func register(player: VideoPlayerModel, for postId: String)
    func setActivePost(_ postId: String, context: PlaybackContext)
    func pause(context: PlaybackContext)
    func resume(context: PlaybackContext)
}
This way your video views aren't hard-coupled to VideoPlaybackManager.shared and become testable/previewable.

For video UI in the redesign, keep the full-screen reels view separate from inline feed cards — you already have this separation but make it explicit in the folder structure.

7. Folder Structure for the Redesign

SaySo/
  App/
    SaySoApp.swift
    AppContainer.swift        ← NEW: DI root
    AppRoutes.swift
  
  Core/
    Networking/
      Apollo/                 ← GraphQL client setup
      GraphQL/                ← Generated types (Apollo codegen)
    Services/
      Analytics/
      PushNotification/
      VideoPlayback/
  
  Domain/                     ← NEW: Pure Swift, no framework deps
    Models/
      Post.swift              ← Domain model (not GQL, not UI)
      User.swift
      Digest.swift
    UseCases/
      Feed/
        FetchDigestUseCase.swift
        FetchExploreUseCase.swift
      Post/
        LikePostUseCase.swift
        SharePostUseCase.swift
        CreatePostUseCase.swift
      Auth/
        SignInUseCase.swift
  
  Data/                       ← NEW: Repository implementations
    Repositories/
      PostRepository.swift
      UserRepository.swift
      DigestRepository.swift
    DataSources/
      Remote/
        GraphQL/PostGraphQLDataSource.swift
      Local/
        DraftStorageDataSource.swift
    Mappers/
      PostMapper.swift
      UserMapper.swift
  
  Features/
    Auth/
    Feed/                     ← renamed from Home
      View/
      ViewModel/
    VideoPlayer/
    Profile/
    CreatePost/
    Explore/
  
  DesignSystem/               ← NEW: moved out of SharedUI
    Tokens/
    Components/
  
  SharedUI/                   ← keep for app-specific shared views
  SharedUtils/
8. How to Actually Start — Recommended Sequence
Phase 1: Foundation (do this before any UI work)

Define domain models (Post, User, Digest) — separate from GQL and UI types
Define repository protocols (PostRepositoryProtocol, etc.)
Set up AppContainer with DI
Build the design token system (Colors, Typography, Spacing)
Phase 2: Data Layer
5. Set up Apollo iOS (or wrap current AppSyncClient in protocols)
6. Implement repositories backed by existing services (you can migrate incrementally)
7. Write use cases on top of repositories

Phase 3: Redesign Screens (one at a time)
8. Start with the simplest screen (Profile or a single onboarding step)
9. Build new @Observable ViewModel consuming a use case
10. Redesign the SwiftUI view using design tokens
11. Repeat for each feature

Phase 4: Video & Feed
12. Redesign the feed card component using design tokens
13. Integrate the existing video infrastructure with the new injectable pattern
14. Tackle the full-screen reels view last since it's the most complex

Key Tradeoffs to Decide Before Starting
Decision	Options	Recommendation
GraphQL client	Keep custom / Switch to Apollo	Apollo — the codegen safety is worth it
State management	Stay on ObservableObject / Move to @Observable	@Observable if iOS 17+ deployment target
Navigation	Keep coordinator / Switch to typed routes	Keep coordinators, but type-safe them with enums
Migration strategy	Big bang rewrite / Incremental	Incremental — feature by feature
Domain models	Reuse UI models / Add domain layer	Add domain layer — the extra indirection pays off
The most important first step is the design token system and the domain model definitions. Everything else can be migrated incrementally without breaking existing functionality.```

slackdump_thread_replies.text:
The restore script inserts rows for tables with `preserveId: false` (like Media) by omitting the `id` column, letting PostgreSQL's auto-increment sequence assign IDs. After restoring hundreds of rows, the sequence advances. But the sequence only tracks what _it_ generated — if the restore is run multiple times or the sequence was already at a value lower than MAX(id), new inserts collide with existing rows.

The real issue: the `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` silently skips duplicate rows during restore, but the sequence *doesn't advance* for skipped rows. After restore, `nextval()` can return an ID that already exists in the table, causing collisions on subsequent application inserts.

I had the resets but removed them in my last commit thinking we won't need them as we're inserting. I didn't think about the skipped rows :man-facepalming:

> PostgreSQL folds unquoted identifiers to lowercase. Your tables were created with double-quoted mixed-case names (e.g. `"Posts"`, `"Media"`), so Postgres stored them as `Posts` not `posts`. Without quotes, `Posts` becomes `posts`, which doesn't exist.
> That's why every table and column with uppercase letters needs double quotes

messages.text:
I wanna set up our repos, to be more inline with claude code and eventually also use these agents to do more async tasks, like certain refactors or bug fixes things like that. I am having trouble in thinking of which direction I should go.
For now I am js going to update the docs, update <http://claude.md|claude.md>, and also add things like agents or skills which can used by devs using CC on local machines
A Couple of Questions I have:
• What all tasks do we want the agents to take care of ?
• What should be the mode in which the agents operate, do we want it to have its own env or should it still work on local machines through terminals
• Setting Documentation and best practices to follow, managing cost (big one)
I think the services repo is a great first candidate, to try things out.
My vision is that we should be able to give it a Task, and it can do all that it needs to and finally js raise a PR which devs can review. It would be on the dev to break down the task and assign it to the agent.
Thoughts?

Couple of Meeting notes from AppSync/MediaPipeline Review session
• Refactor of all resolvers to follow consistent patterns of input, caching sequilize models, different files within a folder (handler, queries, types ...).

• API naming convention: follow Apollo naming standards
• Caching : Ability to cache creator profiles, Digests, Topic Digests
• Backward Compatibility: Make new resolvers instead of replacing older ones
• Media Pipeline : make AWS Tagging optional, Add monitoring
• Repo Organization: ETL, <http://Customer.io|Customer.io> Sync, Analytics are starting to bloat services repo, we should have them in a different repo, to keep deployment cleaner

Hi <@U06JQHRF6HJ> <@U06TP3HRUKV>, About the options to separate v1 and v2 schema: neither GraphQL nor AWS AppSync offer a built-in feature. It seems it is actually considered an antipattern to implement REST-style versioning (e.g., `/v1/posts`) in GraphQL.
The recommended options are either to continue using a v2 suffix or to create a new API if it is a major refactor.

<@U06JQHRF6HJ>
quick one on the Sentry side —

i think you wanted start() to come from AppStartup like the others, but Sentry has to fire really early to catch crashes during everything that runs before AppStartup gets a turn — Facebook, Push, AppsFlyer registration, SwiftUI scene boot, etc. if it only runs from AppStartup we miss all of that. what i have now: start() in AppDelegate's first line for the early coverage, AppStartup just reads the diagnostics it produced. was thinking we could also call start() from AppStartup directly — it's idempotent, the second call is a no-op + returns the cached diagnostics. that way AppStartup reads symmetrically with the other services, but AppDelegate still does the actual early init.

Works for you or you want a different shape?

```- uses: anthropics/claude-code-action@v1

Would like to get inputs on how to structure the review-prompt.md. Initial take:
```You are a code reviewer. Review this PR.

Review against these standards:

## Code Quality
- Minimal and pragmatic — no over-engineering, no premature abstractions
- No unnecessary config, or "just in case" code
- Readability over cleverness
- Follow language style guides

## Security (OWASP Top 10)
- Input validation at system boundaries
- No hardcoded secrets, credentials, or API keys
- No injection vulnerabilities (SQL, XSS, command injection)
- Parameterized queries for database access

Format your response as a GitHub PR comment in markdown with EXACTLY these section headers:

### Must Fix
Critical issues that must be resolved before merging. Number each item. If none, write "None."

### Should Consider
Important improvements that should be addressed. Number each item. If none, write "None."

### Minor
Non-blocking nits and style suggestions. These will NOT be auto-fixed.

### Looks Good
What the PR does well.

Be concise. Flag real problems, skip trivial nitpicks.```

messages.text:
Abut PR stacks: Each PR stack creates its own Cognito user pool, which means we have to create a new test user for every stack to validate the changes, then the pool is destroyed when the PR is closed, but because every PR stack shares the stg database, the user entry in the db and anything that the user produced during the testing stay behind as orphans pointing at a cognitoId that no longer exists anywhere. I see two options:
• keep working this way, or 
• reuse the stg Cognito user pool across PR stacks.
Thoughts? I don't recall if there was a specific reason to create a separate cognito pool per stack.

attachments.text:
I gave it the following task:

```
We want to add support for search synonyms and aliases for SaySo. Start with a plan only and do not edit files yet.

Think holistically:
- whether this belongs in tnm-aws-platform or an application repo
- long-term platform implications
- cost implications
- how this affects future search design
- whether this creates a reusable pattern or a one-off
- what alternatives exist

```

and it produced the following plan:
Search Synonyms & Aliases for SaySo 

*Context*

SaySo's search today is Postgres `ILIKE` substring matching on three resolvers  
(<src/appsync-resolvers/v2/client/search/|v2/client/search/>):
• `searchPosts` → `posts.caption ILIKE %q%`
• `searchTopics` → `topics.name ILIKE %q%`
• `searchUsers` → `users.username ILIKE %q% OR users.name ILIKE %q%`
A user typing "AI" finds nothing about "artificial intelligence"; "POTUS" misses  
"president"; "DJT" misses "Donald Trump". The goal is *user-facing search recall*:  
expand the query into known synonym/alias terms before hitting the database.

*Strategic context (informs scope, not the implementation)*

• The platform repo (`tnm-aws-platform`) has provisioned an OpenSearch Serverless  
`content-search` collection (<../../../tnm-aws-platform/src/domains/sayso/search/OpenSearchConstruct.ts#L207|OpenSearchConstruct.ts:207>)  
with a `synonym_filter` baked into the analyzer  
(<../../../tnm-aws-platform/src/lambda/opensearch/opensearch-index-manager/index.js#L273-L276|opensearch-index-manager/index.js:273-276>),  
but it is *dormant — no data flowing*, and SaySo's resolvers do not consume it.  
We treat OpenSearch as future work and do *not* build against it here.
• The synonym format we choose is intentionally compatible with OpenSearch's native  
`synonym` filter (comma-separated terms per group), so if/when the OpenSearch  
migration revives, the same vocabulary file can be lifted into analyzer config.
• Decision: *SaySo-only, engineer-managed via PR, lives in this repo*. No platform  
changes, no new infrastructure, no new database tables, no admin UI.

*Approach*

Build a static synonym/alias dictionary as a TypeScript module in  
`src/appsync-resolvers/shared/`, and call a pure `expandQuery()` helper from each of  
the three search resolvers to convert the raw user query into a set of OR'd `ILIKE`  
clauses against the existing columns.

*Vocabulary format*

Two complementary structures, both compile-time constants:
• *Synonym groups* — bidirectional. Any term in a group matches the others.  
Format mirrors OpenSearch's `synonym` filter so a future port is mechanical.  
export const SYNONYM_GROUPS: ReadonlyArray<ReadonlyArray<string>> = [  
  ['ai', 'artificial intelligence', 'machine learning', 'ml'],  
  ['eu', 'european union'],  
  ['potus', 'president of the united states'],  
  // ...  
]
• *Aliases* — directional, `alias → canonical`. Use when there's a clear canonical  
form (typically a Topic name or proper noun) we want to bias toward.  
export const ALIASES: Record<string, string> = {  
  djt: 'donald trump',  
  aoc: 'alexandria ocasio-cortez',  
  // ...  
}
Internally both collapse into the same expansion table for lookup; the split exists  
purely so engineers writing entries can express intent (group vs. canonicalize).

*Query expansion*

A single pure function in <src/appsync-resolvers/shared/search-synonyms.ts|search-synonyms.ts>:

export function expandQuery(rawQuery: string): string[]

Behavior:
1. Trim + lowercase the query.
2. Look up the whole query string in the expansion table.
3. Return `[normalizedQuery, ...expansions]`, de-duplicated, original first.
4. If no match, return `[normalizedQuery]` (1-element array — callers always  
iterate, so the path with no synonyms is identical to today's behavior).
*Phase 1 deliberately does NOT tokenize multi-word queries.* Whole-phrase match  
only. Tokenized per-word expansion ("donald trump biden" → expand each token)  
adds noise and is a fast-follow if we see search-quality data demanding it. We  
revisit after instrumenting `search_no_results` events from the iOS client  
(already tracked, per <src/appsync-resolvers/v2/client/search/|Phase 1 exploration>).

*Resolver wiring*

Each of the three handlers does the same shape of change: derive an array of  
search terms once, then change the Sequelize `where` clause from a single  
`ILIKE` to `Op.or` over the expanded terms.
*Posts* — <src/appsync-resolvers/v2/client/search/posts/handler.ts|v2/client/search/posts/handler.ts> and <src/appsync-resolvers/v2/client/search/posts/queries.ts|v2/client/search/posts/queries.ts>:

const terms = expandQuery(rawQuery).map(t => `%${t}%`)
// queries.ts:
where: {
  [Op.or]: terms.map(t => ({ caption: { [Op.iLike]: t } })),
  status: 'PUBLISHED',
  moderationStatus: MediaModerationStatus.APPROVED,
  banned: false,
  ...(blockedUserIds.length > 0 && { userId: { [Op.notIn]: blockedUserIds } }),
}

*Topics* — <src/appsync-resolvers/v2/client/search/topics/handler.ts|v2/client/search/topics/handler.ts>:  
single column (`name`); same `Op.or` shape.
*Users* — <src/appsync-resolvers/v2/client/search/users/handler.ts|v2/client/search/users/handler.ts>:  
two columns (`username`, `name`) and existing `Op.or`. Inner OR becomes the  
cross-product `terms × columns`:

[Op.or]: terms.flatMap(t => [
  { username: { [Op.iLike]: t } },
  { name: { [Op.iLike]: t } },
])

`findAndCountAll` (posts) and `findAll` (topics/users) semantics are preserved;  
`count` and `contributorsCount` still reflect the full expanded query set, which  
is the desired behavior.

*What stays the same*

• GraphQL schema — no changes.
• Pagination (`limit + 1` cursor pattern), `nextToken` encoding, ordering by  
`publishedAt DESC`.
• Authorization, block filtering, moderation gates.
• AppSync wiring in <lib/constructs/AppSyncDataSources.ts|AppSyncDataSources.ts>.

*Cost & performance*

• *No infrastructure cost.* Pure code change.
• *Query cost:* each expansion adds an OR-clause `ILIKE` on the same column.  
At current scale (no production traffic data, but tables are small) Postgres  
will seq-scan + filter regardless of clause count — ILIKE substring queries  
do not use the existing btree indexes. Worst case ~5-10x expansion factor on  
typical synonym entries; query plan stays linear in clause count.
• *Forward path:* when query volume justifies it, add a `pg_trgm` GIN index  
on `posts.caption`, `topics.name`, `users.name`, `users.username`. Each `ILIKE`  
clause can then use the index; expansion remains forward-compatible. This is  
the cheapest performance win and orthogonal to the synonym work — track it  
separately.

*Files to change*

| File                                                       | Change                                                                              |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| <src/appsync-resolvers/shared/search-synonyms.ts>          | *New.* SYNONYM_GROUPS, ALIASES, expandQuery(). Seed with ~15-30 high-value entries. |
| <src/appsync-resolvers/shared/search-synonyms.test.ts>     | *New.* Unit tests for expandQuery.                                                  |
| <src/appsync-resolvers/v2/client/search/posts/queries.ts>  | Accept terms: string[] instead of searchTerm: string; build Op.or clause.           |
| <src/appsync-resolvers/v2/client/search/posts/handler.ts>  | Call expandQuery(rawQuery) and pass terms to query.                                 |
| <src/appsync-resolvers/v2/client/search/topics/handler.ts> | Same pattern (inline query).                                                        |
| <src/appsync-resolvers/v2/client/search/users/handler.ts>  | Same pattern; cross-product over username + name.                                   |

No schema changes, no migrations, no CDK changes, no platform-repo changes.

*Reuse check*

Existing utilities in <src/appsync-resolv…

guard session.isSignedIn else { throw ... }
```

That blocks every guest `PutRecords` call, including the events your DEV-927 stamps with `anon_id`.

My DEV-941 drops that guard so guest credentials are accepted. Once it merges, your stamping reaches Kinesis.

Plan:

I drop my `anon_id` commit from DEV-941 — yours in DEV-927 is cleaner:
  - uses `AnalyticsIdentity` struct
  - has `rotate/clearIdentity`
  - lock-safe

DEV-941 merges first with just the root-cause fixes:
  - resolver guard
  - boot-time configure
  - foreground flush
  - lifecycle idempotency
You rebase DEV-927 on top.

Guest credentials now resolve, so your `anon_id` stamping reaches Kinesis end-to-end.

Sound good?

Hey <@U05BV05GYQH>, working on <https://app.asana.com/1/1206660498759239/project/1211854325083548/task/1214542735108150?focus=true|DEV-1138> (refresh-token expiry on launch).

Before fix: user saw a blocking "Analytics unavailable / AuthError 7" modal and got stuck on Main with no way forward. After: no modal, the app force-logs them out to landing with a clear "Session expired" alert so they can sign in again. The fix itself solves the UX, but we still have no prod signal for this bug. So I'm thinking it'd be right to add a `session_expired` lifecycle event (same pattern as `user_signout`, stamped with the outgoing user_id) — so we can measure how often users actually hit this post-fix and triage if reports keep coming in.

Two questions:

  1. OK to add it?
  2. If yes — Marin suggested Kinesis-only (not AppsFlyer) since it's diagnostic, not attribution. Sound right?

Happy to drop if it doesn't fit your direction.

(refresh-token expiry on launch).

Before fix: user saw a blocking "Analytics unavailable / AuthError 7" modal and got stuck on Main with no way forward. After: no modal, the app force-logs them out to landing with a clear "Session expired" alert so they can sign in again. The fix itself solves the UX, but we still have no prod signal for this bug. So I'm thinking it'd be right to add a
session_expired
lifecycle event (same pattern as
user_signout

, stamped with the outgoing user_id) — so we can measure how often users actually hit this post-fix and triage if reports keep coming in.

Two questions:

  1. OK to add it?
  2. If yes — Marin suggested Kinesis-only (not AppsFlyer) since it's diagnostic, not attribution. Sound right?

Happy to drop if it doesn't fit your direction.
